title: Design SDK Component Usage Contract (guard.json)
description: Machine-readable usage contract shipped beside a component family. It tells a code-generating LLM the component's intended usage so it stops guessing: what the component is for, when to reach for something else, its default prop values, its size axis (or fixed metrics), its keyboard/ARIA model, which prop combinations are illegal, how sub-components legally nest, and canonical correct vs incorrect snippets. Soft/guidance enforcement — not a runtime or type system. AUTHORING ORDER (JSON keys are unordered at parse time, but author sections in this canonical order so every guard reads the same): component → import → purpose → useInstead → decision → defaults → sizing → accessibility → propRules → composition → subComponents → variants → sectionEditing → antiPatterns → examples.

$schema.description: Relative path to this schema, for editor validation.

component.description: The family-root component name (e.g. Table, Chart, Card, TopNav, SideNavBar). Must match the guard file basename — Table.guard.json -> "Table".

import.description: The canonical import specifier for the family root (e.g. "@faclon-labs/design-sdk/Table").

purpose.description: One-line statement of what this component is for. The first thing an LLM reads to decide whether to use it.

useInstead.description: Disambiguation map — when NOT to use this component and what to reach for instead.

when.description: The situation the LLM might be in.

use.description: The component/pattern to use for that situation instead.

decision.description: The DECISION LAYER (migrated from the FDS decision docs, 2026-08-26): how an AI chooses this component and its prop values, as staged, ordered, confidence-graded rules. Resolve stages in `order`, never reordered; within a stage the FIRST rule whose `if` matches wins; `collisions` names the exceptions. This section is the authority for selection/axis decisions — where it is silent, say so rather than borrowing a rule from another design system.

authority.description: The authority claim, e.g. 'This guard is the authority for Button decisions in this design system.'

aliases.description: 'Also called' names (CTA, push button, …) so retrieval finds the page from a user's vocabulary.

order.description: The traversal stages (e.g. Selection → Emphasis → Meaning → Density → Icons → Overrides), resolved in sequence. Every rule's `stage` must be one of these.

beforeTheRules.description: The pre-questions the rules assume answered — usually whether this component is the right shape at all. Read before the rules.

rules.description: Numbered decision rules, in document order. First match per stage wins.

confidence.description: High: if the If matches, the Then is not arguable. Medium: the trigger needs judgment, or the outcome is one defensible answer among several — the rule says which.

why.description: The rule's own rationale line, where the doc gives one.

collisions.description: What wins when rules/constraints/patterns collide. A named winner here overrides rule numbering.

between.description: The colliding parties — rule ids, or short names for constraints/patterns.

winner.description: The winning rule id or constraint name, when one side simply wins.

constraints.description: What you cannot change (the doc's section 4) — invariants no rule may override unless a collision row says so.

propGuide.description: 'Every prop, and when to reach for it' — the answer when the prop is known and the question is whether it applies.

situations.description: Worked situations (the doc's section 6): a concrete intent resolved through the stages.

certainty.description: How sure to be and what is missing (the doc's section 9) — the honest edges of the rules' coverage.

defaults.description: Resolved default value per key prop (e.g. { "mode": "single", "leading": "None" }) — what the component does when the prop is omitted. LLMs guess defaults constantly; this ends that. Only list props whose default materially changes behaviour or appearance.

sizing.description: The component's size axis — or the statement that there isn't one. sizeProp: null means a single fixed size (do NOT invent a size prop); metrics lists the real fixed dimensions/tokens so an LLM doesn't restyle them.

sizeProp.description: The prop that selects the size (e.g. "size"), or null when the component ships a single fixed size.

options.description: The legal size values with their key dimension (e.g. "Medium (36px field)", "Large (48px field)").

default.description: The default size value when sizeProp is present.

metrics.description: Fixed dimensions/typography/tokens (e.g. "header padding 16px (--spacing-05)", "title BodyMediumMedium"). These are locked by the design system.

accessibility.description: The keyboard map and ARIA wiring — including explicit limitations (e.g. "no Arrow-key roving") so an LLM neither re-implements nor over-promises behaviour.

keyboard.description: Key → behaviour lines (e.g. "Enter/Space — toggle the focused header"). Include what the component does NOT do.

aria.description: ARIA roles/attributes the component wires up (and when they're omitted).

propRules.description: Machine-readable prop-combination rules on the family root. Same when/require/forbid shape as the SDK's dev-mode console.warn checks so the two can share a source later.

composition.description: How the component's children must be shaped, plus root-level structural rules.

requiredParent.description: A component that must wrap this one (e.g. SideNavBar requires SideNavBarProvider). null when free-standing.

childrenContract.description: The SHAPE of children, read before the sub-component tree. none: the component renders no children at all. text: children is a text label. single-element: exactly one element, cloned rather than wrapped. render-prop: children is a function. slots: children are specific named sub-components. provider-wrapped: must be wrapped in a context provider. free: any ReactNode.

childrenSignature.description: For render-prop contracts, the function signature (e.g. "(rows: Item[]) => ReactNode").

notes.description: Free-text structural guidance (e.g. "Plain JSX children are a TypeScript error").

rules.description: Structural invariants that aren't single-prop rules (e.g. every data node needs a unique id).

subComponents.description: The legal nesting tree — every sub-component of the family with its role, parent, allowed children and multiplicity. This is the dominant guardrail for composition-heavy families.

name.description: Exported sub-component name (must be a real export).

role.description: One-line description of what it does.

parent.description: The component it must nest directly under (e.g. "TableHeaderRow"). Omit for the family root or wrapper-level entries.

children.description: Sub-components this one may contain directly.

keyProps.description: Props the LLM must set for this sub-component to work (e.g. TableHeaderCell needs headerKey + sortFunction).

multiplicity.description: How many may appear under the parent.

propRules.description: Prop rules scoped to this sub-component (used by Chart for its per-type wrappers).

variants.description: Named, story-backed usage variants of the component, each with its own rules and example (e.g. a full card, a no-padding full-bleed card, a metric/KPI card, a scrollable card). A variant is a recognised way to use the SAME component — not a separate component.

when.description: The situation/intent this variant applies to.

description.description: What the variant is and how it differs.

recommendedProps.description: Typical prop values for this variant (e.g. { size: 'medium', padding: 'spacing.5' }).

sectionEditing.description: Per-section editing guardrails — for each editable region of the component, what props can be edited, which children are allowed, and which props are intentionally LOCKED (so an LLM doesn't fight fixed sizes/variants).

editableProps.description: Props that are safe to set/change on this section.

lockedProps.description: Props intentionally fixed by the design system — do not try to override (e.g. "CardHeaderBadge.size=Medium"). To go off-spec, drop to the raw primitive.

antiPatterns.description: Explicit do/don't pairs — the highest-signal guidance for an LLM.

why.description: Why the wrong one is wrong.

examples.description: Canonical correct usage plus common wrong snippets.

additional.description: Further named examples beyond the canonical one — key is a short scenario name, value is the code.

severity.description: error = never do this; warn = discouraged.

when.description: Trigger condition — prop values that activate the rule. Use "*" as a value to mean "any value present".

require.description: Props/attributes that MUST also be set when `when` matches.

forbid.description: Prop -> list of values that are NOT allowed when `when` matches.
